Question: Is the “ability to consummate” concept subject to Material Adverse Effect (MAE) carveouts?
Option A: No
Option B: Yes

Merger Agreement: “Company Material Adverse Effect” means any occurrence, change, event, or combination thereof that (a) has, or would reasonably be expected to have, a material adverse impact on the business, operations, assets, or results of operations of the Company and its Subsidiaries, or (b) would, individually or in aggregate with other such occurrences, materially impair or delay the ability of the Company to consummate the Transaction. Notwithstanding the foregoing, and without limiting the generality of the definition, no such occurrence shall be deemed a Company Material Adverse Effect if it arises solely from: (i) changes in general economic conditions or industry-wide trends affecting all participants in the market, (ii) modifications in GAAP or other accounting principles adopted uniformly by industry peers, or (iii) fluctuations in market conditions, including stock price or trading volume, unless such fluctuations exhibit a disproportionate adverse impact compared to industry benchmarks. Moreover, any delay in consummation specifically attributable to regulatory approvals or non-material procedural adjustments shall not be considered under this definition. It is expressly provided, however, that the “ability to consummate” requirement, as a standard for the Transaction’s success, is not mitigated by the aforementioned carveouts and remains fully operative in identifying occurrences that materially affect the timing or feasibility of the Transaction.
